signature.name: VTask.Equilateral
signature.type: {R : Type u_1} -> {V : Type u_2} -> {P : Type u_3} -> [Ring R] -> [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] -> [PseudoMetricSpace P] -> [Module R V] -> [NormedAddTorsor V P] -> {n : ℕ} -> (s : Affine.Simplex R P n) -> Prop

conventions.statement: The common edge length r may be zero; a degenerate simplex with all vertices at the same point satisfies VTask.Equilateral with r = 0.
conventions.note: No restriction on r in the existential

conventions.statement: A 0-simplex (single vertex) has no pairs of distinct vertices, so VTask.Equilateral holds vacuously for every 0-simplex.
A 1-simplex has exactly one pair of distinct vertices, so VTask.Equilateral holds for every 1-simplex by taking r to be that single edge length.

facts.statement: ∀ {R : Type*} {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring R] [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] [PseudoMetricSpace P] [Module R V] [NormedAddTorsor V P] {n : ℕ} (s : Affine.Simplex R P n), s.Regular → VTask.Equilateral s

facts.statement: ∀ {R : Type*} {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring R] [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] [PseudoMetricSpace P] [Module R V] [NormedAddTorsor V P] {n : ℕ} (s : Affine.Simplex R P n), VTask.Equilateral s → ∀ {i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ : Fin (n + 1)}, i₁ ≠ i₂ → i₃ ≠ i₄ → dist (s.points i₁) (s.points i₂) = dist (s.points i₃) (s.points i₄)
